This image captures a dynamic spirograph pattern rendered through light painting, using a red LED as the sole light source. Executed with a Canon EOS 800D at a 30-second exposure, the photograph visualizes hypotrochoid curve traced in midair. The rotational motion and geometric precision reflect the interplay between mathematical order and organic adaptation, offering a visual metaphor for cyclical processes in nature.

Belem, Berardo Collection, Centro Cultural de Belem, Lisbon, Portugal Material : Painted nails on wood BIOGRAPHY From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Günther Uecker, also known as Guenther Uecker, (born 13 March 1930) is a German sculptor, op artist and installation artist. Uecker was born in Wendorf, Mecklenburg. Uecker began his artistic education in 1949 when he took up studies at Wismar. He then went to the art school in Berlin-Weißensee and in 1955 to Düsseldorf, where he studied under Otto Pankok at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf. In 1956 he began using nails in his art. source_title: Man photographing himself in hotel bathroom with mirrors all around to generate illusion
desc_src: Man photographing himself in a cornered mirror to generate a multiple reflection. On the right border, the front side of the smartphone used is visible, with the lens seemingly pointing to the viewer. This is the first reflection of the phone in the first mirror, wherein the mirror is virtually placed between the smartphone and the viewer. The man taking the pic (the same as 'the others' in the pic) would, as his first reflection, also look in the direction of the viewer, but is standing 'outside of the window frame'.
